rationale: A wins because it gives the founder five genuinely different reporting lanes and, more importantly, tells them which ones are hostile territory before they walk into the room. Its lock-in angle, "The more Toast a restaurant buys, the harder it is to leave," is a real market-power story B simply leaves on the floor. B's opener, "Toast crosses 120,000 restaurant locations as it pivots from hardware to fintech margins," tries to make one angle carry category, markets, and margin-quality work; that is how angles get fat and pitches get vague. A has one ugly overclaim, but the set is still sharper strategic material.
gaps_in_A: "Toast reached profitability by selling loans, not hardware" overstates the facts. The update says Toast recently reached profitability and says fintech/lending are higher-margin than hardware; it does not prove loans caused profitability.
"an industry with well-known failure rates" imports an outside claim. If you want restaurant failure rates in the default-risk angle, source them or keep them out.

"Toast lends to restaurants and won't say how many fail to repay" implies refusal. The supplied fact is that default rates are not disclosed; filings still need to be checked before using that framing.
gaps_in_B: "pivots from hardware to fintech margins" is too strong. The update supports bundling and higher-margin fintech, not a clean pivot away from hardware.

"The prevailing belief is that a newly profitable, publicly traded platform lending against its own customers' sales has a clean, well-understood book" is a made-up strawman unless you can point to analysts or filings saying it.
It misses the clean public-markets angle A spotted: margin quality and whether profitability depends on fintech/lending versus hardware. B buries that inside the category angle.

"Toast payroll solves the tipped-vs-hourly staffing headache for operators" is not a duplicate of the cash-advance customer angle. It is a potentially separate labor/payroll-compliance story; the real reason to refuse it is missing proof, not duplicate protagonist.
